body.statement: For each fixed \(n\ge2\), the actual restricted supremum in Definition \(\mathrm{def:radial\text{-}modulus}\) satisfies \(\Omega_{k,m}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp_n\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). The active map is a bounded \(C^k\) radial rotation in the named plane \(E_{12}\), supported on a fixed chart cylinder and equal to the identity on coordinates three through \(n\); therefore the interpolation and Hellinger integrals are two-dimensional, while constants may depend on the fixed \(n\). In particular, the audited \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\) restriction has exponent \(3/4\).
body.justification: This nontrivial infinite-dimensional sector verifies the proposed exponent before the arbitrary-map rigidity step.
body.gap: No inspected causal representation result computes a sharp modulus even on radial nonlinear torus decoders.
body.consumer: The radial theorem supplies a controlled benchmark and a falsifiable testbed for proofs and numerical recovery procedures.
